stances.claim: FLP hails and congratulates its 14 scholars who topped or passed the 2025 bar examinations -- per the SC press briefer, three FLP scholars were among the top 20 passers: ADMU class valedictorian Enrico Gabriel Paguia (6th place), Ignacio Lorenzo Villareal (UP, 15th), and Chinzen Viernes (UP, 19th); 11 other FLP law scholars passed, upholding FLP's 100% passing rate.

Since 2018, FLP -- in partnership with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation -- has been sponsoring a unique, merit-based 'Legal Scholarship Program' that aims to identify and support the best and brightest law students and provides them with resources and opportunities to excel academically, socially, and professionally.

The FLP track record includes several bar toppers -- the 2018 batch was led by Sean James Borja (ADMU, 1st place), Katrina Monica Gaw (ADMU, 5th), and Ervin Fredrick Dy (UP, 17th); 2019 had Kenneth Glenn Manuel (UST, 6th) and Dexter Rojas (PUP, 9th); 2022 had Louis-Mari Opina (UST, 19th); and 2024 had Kyle Christian Tutor (UP, 1st place), Maria Lovelyn Joyce Quebrar (UP, 6th), and Betlee-kyle Barraquias (ADMU, 18th).

Notably, the SC did not rank the Top 20 passers in the 2020-2021 bar exams amid the pandemic, opting instead to recognize 'exemplary' (85-90% average) and 'excellent' (above 90%) performances -- three FLP scholars achieved excellent performance: Stephanie Mae Domingo (Cordilleras), Geremae Mata (USC), and Jani Omamalin (USC).

CJP praises retired SAJ Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe (FLP trustee) for being the 2025 civil-law examiner, and personal friends who were likewise bar examiners -- Judge Cherry Chiara L. Hernando (commercial/tax), SBN Justice Sarah Jane T. Fernandez (criminal), and retired CA Justice Magdangal M. De Leon (labor/social legislation).

The loudest clap belongs to Justice Amy C. Lazaro-Javier, overall chair of the 2025 bar exams -- history will long remember her headship and, more importantly, her authorship of Pimentel v. House (Dec 3 2025) holding that PhilHealth monies belong to its contributors and cannot be transferred to the National Treasury, much less fund 'wantonly fraudulent public works projects.'

stances.claim: Lawyering is invested with public interest, and lawyers are regarded and disciplined by the SC as public officers -- our profession serves as the first key to the justice system; whenever people encounter legal problems, the first experts available to help them are bar exam passers.

While topping the bar does not guarantee future success or exceptional skill, history shows many top-20 passers become leading practitioners, professors, corporate counsels, and public officials -- they are highly sought after and well-compensated, but achievement always comes with the burdens of responsibility and expectations of integrity.

It is CJP's fervent hope that FLP scholars will carry the foundation's philosophy wherever their legal careers take them -- safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity under the rule of law are not merely abstract ideals but practical guides that should inform every decision, every case, and every client interaction throughout their careers.

It is CJP's deepest prayer that our country will produce more enlightened, well-trained, and principled lawyers who will dedicate their lives and careers to competent and ethical practice -- excellence demonstrated through exams is obvious and easily measured, but ethics is not always so apparent; ethical practice in law lies not just in doing what is right but in consistently serving and uplifting many Filipinos, especially the marginalized and the poor.

Earning the title 'Attorney' is only the beginning -- how new lawyers uphold integrity, competence, and service will be judged by time; the title itself can be revoked through disbarment for gross misconduct, a sober reminder that great privilege carries great responsibility. The bar exam is merely the beginning; what comes beyond is a journey that will define not only their career but also their steadfast commitment to liberty, prosperity, and the rule of law.

one_paragraph_summary: FLP congratulates its 14 scholars who topped or passed the 2025 bar examinations, led by ADMU class valedictorian Enrico Gabriel Paguia (6th place) and two UP placers (Villareal 15th, Viernes 19th), with 11 other passers from UP, Bulacan State, USC, Xavier, and ADMU upholding FLP's 100% passing rate. Panganiban recaps the program's track record since 2018 -- including 1st-placer Sean James Borja (2018) and Kyle Christian Tutor (2024) -- and commends the 2025 bar examiners as well as overall chair Justice Amy C. Lazaro-Javier, whose authorship of Pimentel v. House (Dec 3 2025) ruled that PhilHealth funds belong to contributors and cannot fund 'wantonly fraudulent public works.' He closes with the reminder that lawyering is invested with public interest, that the Attorney title can be revoked by disbarment, and that ethics -- not just exam excellence -- defines the safeguarding of liberty and nurturing of prosperity under the rule of law.
